languages.name: C++
languages.description: Modern C++ reference focused on RAII, generic programming, STL, concurrency, and systems/application tooling.

categories.name: Core Modern C++
categories.description: References, classes, value semantics, and RAII.

entries.title: References
entries.summary: Create aliases to existing objects with T& or const T&.
entries.definition: Create aliases to existing objects with T& or const T&.
entries.mental_model: A non-null alias with language-level binding semantics.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: Classes
entries.summary: Define types with encapsulated state and behavior.
entries.definition: Define types with encapsulated state and behavior.
entries.mental_model: State + invariants + behavior under one nominal type.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Defines a class with private state.

entries.title: RAII
entries.summary: Tie resource lifetime to object lifetime so destructors release resources automatically.
entries.definition: Tie resource lifetime to object lifetime so destructors release resources automatically.
entries.mental_model: Scope exit becomes the universal cleanup trigger.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::ifstream file("README.md");
// closes automatically when file leaves scope

entries.title: Move semantics
entries.summary: Transfer resources from expiring objects instead of copying them.
entries.definition: Transfer resources from expiring objects instead of copying them.
entries.mental_model: Reuse ownership of expensive buffers rather than duplicate them.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::string a = "Wyn";
std::string b = std::move(a);

entries.title: const correctness
entries.summary: Express whether functions/references may modify objects.
entries.definition: Express whether functions/references may modify objects.
entries.mental_model: Mutability is part of the interface contract.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: std::size_t length(const std::string& s) { return s.size(); }

categories.name: STL and Generic Programming
categories.description: Containers, algorithms, iterators, lambdas, and templates.

entries.title: std::vector
entries.summary: Store a growable contiguous sequence.
entries.definition: Store a growable contiguous sequence.
entries.mental_model: The default dynamic array of modern C++.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::vector<std::string> keys{"M1", "M2"};
keys.push_back("M3");

entries.title: std::unordered_map
entries.summary: Store hash-based key-value mappings.
entries.definition: Store hash-based key-value mappings.
entries.mental_model: Average constant-time lookup with key hashing.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: std::unordered_map<std::string,std::string> m{{"M4","Zig"}};

entries.title: Templates
entries.summary: Parameterize code over types or compile-time values.
entries.definition: Parameterize code over types or compile-time values.
entries.mental_model: Generate type-specialized code from one abstraction.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
template <typename T>
T twice(T x) { return x + x; }

entries.title: Lambdas
entries.summary: Create anonymous function objects with explicit capture syntax.
entries.definition: Create anonymous function objects with explicit capture syntax.
entries.mental_model: Compiler-generated callable object with controlled captures.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
int factor = 2;
auto scale = [factor](int x) { return x * factor; };

entries.title: Algorithms
entries.summary: Apply generic operations such as sort, find, transform, and accumulate over iterator ranges.
entries.definition: Apply generic operations such as sort, find, transform, and accumulate over iterator ranges.
entries.mental_model: Algorithms operate on ranges instead of owning containers.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::vector<int> v{3,1,2};
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());

entries.title: Ranges
entries.summary: Compose modern range views and algorithms with less iterator ceremony.
entries.definition: Compose modern range views and algorithms with less iterator ceremony.
entries.mental_model: Lazy range adaptors build transformation pipelines.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: auto even = values | std::views::filter([](int n){ return n % 2 == 0; });

categories.name: Ownership, Errors, and Files
categories.description: Smart pointers, exceptions, filesystem, and optional values.

entries.title: std::unique_ptr
entries.summary: Own a heap object exclusively with automatic deletion.
entries.definition: Own a heap object exclusively with automatic deletion.
entries.mental_model: Single-owner RAII for dynamic objects.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: auto p = std::make_unique<int>(42);
examples.explanation: Allocates an integer with exclusive ownership.

entries.title: std::shared_ptr
entries.summary: Share ownership through reference counting.
entries.definition: Share ownership through reference counting.
entries.mental_model: Object lifetime ends when the final shared owner disappears.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
auto p = std::make_shared<int>(42);
auto q = p;
examples.explanation: Shares ownership between two smart pointers.

entries.title: Exceptions
entries.summary: Signal failures by throwing objects and handle them with catch.
entries.definition: Signal failures by throwing objects and handle them with catch.
entries.mental_model: Stack unwinding runs destructors while searching for a handler.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: try { throw std::runtime_error("bad"); } catch (const std::exception& e) { std::cerr << e.what(); }

entries.title: std::optional
entries.summary: Represent a value that may be absent.
entries.definition: Represent a value that may be absent.
entries.mental_model: Explicit optional presence without sentinel values.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::optional<int> value = 42;
if (value) std::cout << *value;

entries.title: std::filesystem
entries.summary: Manipulate paths and filesystem entries portably.
entries.definition: Manipulate paths and filesystem entries portably.
entries.mental_model: Filesystem paths become typed values.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
namespace fs = std::filesystem;
fs::path p = fs::path("packs") / "cpp.json";

entries.title: std::thread
entries.summary: Launch operating-system threads.
entries.definition: Launch operating-system threads.
entries.mental_model: A movable RAII-ish handle to native thread execution.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::thread t([] { std::cout << "worker"; });
t.join();

entries.title: std::mutex
entries.summary: Serialize access to shared mutable state.
entries.definition: Serialize access to shared mutable state.
entries.mental_model: Mutual exclusion plus RAII locking.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
std::mutex m;
{ std::lock_guard lock(m); /* protected */ }

entries.title: Concepts
entries.summary: Constrain templates with named compile-time requirements.
entries.definition: Constrain templates with named compile-time requirements.
entries.mental_model: Readable predicates over types used by templates.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
template <typename T> concept Number = std::is_arithmetic_v<T>;
template <Number T> T twice(T x) { return x + x; }

entries.title: constexpr
entries.summary: Allow values/functions to be evaluated during compilation when inputs permit.
entries.definition: Allow values/functions to be evaluated during compilation when inputs permit.
entries.mental_model: One function can participate in compile-time or runtime evaluation.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
constexpr int square(int x) { return x * x; }
constexpr int n = square(6);
